title: Scope of Relationship Bonus Already Credited Before a Correction
content:
What is deducted as already credited from the relationship bonus owed on an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts follows the withdrawal history of the account: the count of withdrawals posted to it in the twelve calendar months ending on the review date.

1. Where 5 or more withdrawals posted in that twelve-month window, every relationship bonus amount credited in the three calendar months ending on the review date is deducted.
2. Where 3 or 4 withdrawals posted in that twelve-month window, only the most recently credited relationship bonus amount is deducted.
3. Where fewer than 3 withdrawals posted in that twelve-month window, the relationship bonus credited in the one calendar month ending on the review date is deducted.

### A worked case on hypothetical inputs

Take a savings account whose relationship bonus credits in the three calendar months ending on the review date are 3.00 USD, 2.50 USD and, most recently, 2.00 USD, the last of them falling inside the one calendar month ending on that date.

| Withdrawals in the twelve calendar months ending on the review date | Deducted |
| --- | --- |
| 5 or more | 3.00 USD, 2.50 USD and 2.00 USD together, that is 7.50 USD |
| 3 or 4 | 2.00 USD, the most recently credited amount |
| fewer than 3 | 2.00 USD, being the amount credited in the one calendar month ending on the review date |

In this case the second and third rules reach the same figure because the most recent credit happens to fall inside the one calendar month. Where the most recent relationship bonus credit fell two calendar months before the review date, the second rule would still deduct it and the third would deduct nothing, there being no credit in that one calendar month.

### Boundary of the counts

A count of exactly 5 withdrawals falls under the first rule, a count of exactly 3 under the second, and a count of 2, 1 or 0 under the third.
